slides.0.title: Cape South Coast
slides.0.subtitle: Hemel-en-Aarde, Elgin, Elim
slides.1.title: The Region and its climate
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Two currents
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The cold Benguela Current lies to the west and the warmer Agulhas Current influences the south and east; persistent sea breezes cut afternoon heat and preserve acidity
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Districts
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The text lists seven: Walker Bay, Elgin, Cape Agulhas, Overberg, Plettenberg Bay, Swellendam and Lower Duivenhoks (the infobox lists six)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Signature grapes
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, cool-climate Syrah and Cap Classique
slides.1.content: Keywords for the Cape South Coast: cool, sea breezes, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
slides.2.title: Walker Bay and Hemel-en-Aarde
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Status over time
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A ward of Overberg in 1981, it became a District in May 2004
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Three Hemel-en-Aarde wards
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Hemel-en-Aarde Valley (August 2006, 80–200 m, Bokkeveld shale), Upper Hemel-en-Aarde Valley (August 2006, 200–350 m) and Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge (June 2009, 240–400 m, the highest and most inland)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The pioneer
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Tim Hamilton Russell scouted the valley in 1975, planted in 1976 and made his first wine in 1981
slides.2.content: The further inland and higher, the more the three Hemel-en-Aarde wards differ in style.
slides.3.title: Elgin and Elim
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Elgin
slides.3.highlights.0.content: A cool upland at about 200–400 m with about 1,000 mm of rain; for most of the 20th century it was the largest apple and pear district and wine planting began in the mid-1980s; a Ward of Overberg in 1990 and a stand-alone District in 2011; Chardonnay is the signature
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Elim
slides.3.highlights.1.content: A Ward within the Cape Agulhas District about 15–17 km from the coast, described as Africa's southernmost wine area; the first WO Elim wine was the 1999 Land's End Sauvignon Blanc
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Wind and iron-rich soils
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Persistent wind gives wind-pruned canopies and low yields; ferricrete (koffieklip), quartzite and iron-rich clay are linked to a saline-mineral character
slides.3.content: Elgin relies on height and cool; Elim on wind and iron-rich soils: both are cool-climate standard-bearers of the Cape South Coast.
In which year did Walker Bay become a District?
May 2004; in 1981 it was a ward of Overberg.
Which of the three Hemel-en-Aarde wards is the highest and most inland?
For what crop was Elgin known for most of the 20th century?
Apples and pears; wine grapes only began in the mid-1980s.
